== Ingredients ==
* 2 each boneless skinless [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] thighs, drumsticks, and breasts
* [[Cookbook:Hickory BBQ Rub|Hickory BBQ Rub]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ¾ cup [[Cookbook:Honey|honey]]
* 2 cups hot apple [[Cookbook:Cider Vinegar|cider vinegar]]
* 1 [[Cookbook:Pound|pound]] ice
* 1 cup [[Cookbook:Kansas City Barbecue Sauce|homemade barbecue sauce]]

== Special equipment ==
*2 probe [[Cookbook:Thermometer|thermometers]]
*Hickory wood chips

== Procedure ==
#Combine salt, honey, and vinegar in a gallon size zip-top bag until salt has dissolved. Add ice and shake until ice is almost completely melted and mixture has cooled down. Insert chicken pieces and refrigerate 1½–2 hours, turning once.
#Place a good amount of hickory chips in the bottom of a large roasting pan. Place a roasting rack in that pan. Set aside.
#Drain chicken and discard mixture. Pat dry with [[Cookbook:Paper Towel|paper towels]] and season chicken liberally on both sides with rub. Gently pat into meat and refrigerate for at least 1 hour (more rub will stick if you wear gloves).
#[[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|Toss]] chicken pieces in barbecue sauce. Place on the prepared roasting pan and insert 1 probe thermometer into one of the breasts and one into the thighs. [[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] in the center of a 375°F [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] until both the thigh and the breast's internal temperature reach 165°F.
#Bring remaining sauce to a [[Cookbook:Boiling|boil]] in a large [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium high heat for 5 minutes. Set aside. 
#Remove and cover with [[Cookbook:Aluminium Foil|aluminum foil]]. Let rest 10 minutes. Serve warm with remaining sauce.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Avoid bottled barbecue sauce, which has too much sugar.
